text:
anya: Quick post-mortem from the canary run: we saw a sharp spike in duplicate upstream requests tied to our ACK heuristic. Posting logs + thoughts.

rahul: Which heuristic? the packet-count window or the time-since-last-ack?

anya: Packet-count. Example trace: trace=00-abc123...

anya: logs:
```
[2026-03-20T09:12:01Z] node=ingress-12 route=public-api conn=0x9f ack_missing_packets=3 ack_window=4 triggered_retry=true trace=abc123
[2026-03-20T09:12:01Z] node=ingress-12 upstream=svc-a attempt=1 latency_ms=5 status=200
[2026-03-20T09:12:01Z] node=ingress-12 retry_dispatched=true reason=ack_probe
```

li: Did the client eventually ACK?

anya: Yes ~40ms later, so retry was unnecessary and caused duplicate work. p99 ack-latency for that client cohort is ~95ms.

george: Memory / per-connection/state numbers? If we increase window it'll grow linearly.

anya: Rough calc: avg frame ~1.2KB. window 4 => 4.8KB/sess. window 10 => 12KB/sess. At 60k concurrent sessions that’s ~720MB extra. Heap churn is worse in Go due to many short-lived buffers.

rahul: Alternative: add a soft-hedge: when ack-window triggers, instead of immediate retry, schedule a short randomized probe (10-40ms) that checks if client_seq advanced. If not, issue retry. This keeps window small most of the time.

george: That tradeoff seems good: small p99 increase for massive reduction in duplicate upstream work. But probes still require timer budget per-session. How many timers can node handle?

li: We already have timer shards but not tuned for O(1e5) scheduled jittered probes. Can we batch timers into a wheel or coalesce by bucketed deadlines?

anya: We prototyped a bucketed timer wheel that coalesces probes into 5ms buckets. It reduced timer objects by ~85% in local tests. Implementation cost is moderate but low-risk.

rahul: Observability: add metric labels `retry_reason`, `retry_probe=true`, `client_variant` and emit `ack_probe_latency_ms`. This will let us distinguish false positives from real upstream failures.

george: Also add `retry_attempt` tag to identify thundering herds.

li: One more long-term option: extend the protocol to carry a lightweight progress token from client (progress_seq) so ingress can detect forward progress without buffering frames. That’s cleaner but requires coordinated rollout and isn't viable for Private installs immediately.

anya: Proposal for rollout: 1) enable hedge-probe (10-40ms jitter) behind a feature flag on canaries, 2) keep ack_window=4, 3) implement timer wheel to avoid memory blowup, 4) add metrics/tags, 5) monitor for 72h then consider increasing window if false positives persist.

rahul: +1. Add an alert: if `sum(increase(proxy.retry.count[1m])) > 100` AND `proxy.ack_probe_latency_ms.p99 > 120` then page infra.

george: Also watch upstream error budget — probes should reduce duplicate load so we should see upstream cpu/req_per_sec stabilize.

ops-bot: Deploy plan recorded: https://deploys.internal/redwood/canary/ingress-hedge-probe. CI: unit + integration + load smoke passed.

li: Thanks. Can we also ensure docs and the private-deploy migration note are updated before wide rollout? Some customers will want opt-out config.

anya: Will open PR with the flag, metrics, and migration note. Owners: @anya (runtime), @rahul (observability), @george (infra).
